mainTopic: The rules of זימון, the origins, order and תורה sources of the ברכות of ברכת המזון, the sources for ברכת התורה, and the required wording of ברכת המזון.
overview: This amud begins in the middle of a ruling about זימון. Even someone who ate one dried fig can join the group, but only someone who ate a כזית of grain can be מוציא others, and רבא rules the same way. רב נחמן then traces the history of the four ברכות of ברכת המזון: משה, יהושע, דוד and שלמה, and the חכמים in יבנה after the tragedy of ביתר. A ברייתא gives the order of the ברכות and a מחלוקת about where to mention שבת, and the גמרא explains that the תנא קמא and the חכמים differ only בדיעבד. Another ברייתא learns each ברכה from the פסוק ״וְאָכַלְתָּ וְשָׂבָעְתָּ וּבֵרַכְתָּ״, and several תנאים give different sources for the ברכה before eating. After a short side story about why the maidens spoke at length to שאול, the ברייתא brings sources for ברכת התורה, and רבי מאיר teaches that we bless ה׳ over bad things too. The amud ends with required wording in ברכת המזון: ארץ חמדה טובה ורחבה, מלכות בית דוד, ברית and תורה. פלימו's reason for putting ברית before תורה continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Even a tiny amount of food lets someone join the group
steps.stepSummary: Someone who only dipped food in brine with the group, or ate only a single dried fig, still counts toward the זימון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if he only dipped something in brine with them, and ate with them only one dried fig, he joins the group for זימון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a statement that began on the previous amud. It says a person who ate even a tiny bit with the group can join their זימון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Joining a זימון does not require a full bread meal. Eating any small amount together, even one dried fig, is enough to count as part of the group.

keyTerms.meaning: Brine, the salty liquid used for dipping food
The invitation to say ברכת המזון together as a group

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. The words 'even if' and the speaker's name appear on the previous amud.

phrases.english: (even if) he dipped with them only in brine,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא אָכַל עִמָּהֶם אֶלָּא גְּרוֹגֶרֶת אַחַת —
phrases.english: and ate with them only a single dried fig —
he joins (them for the זימון).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a statement from the previous amud about the minimum eating needed to join a זימון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating even a minimal amount, such as one dried fig, is enough to join a זימון.

steps.title: Being מוציא others requires a כזית of grain
steps.stepSummary: Although a tiny amount lets him join, he cannot lead and be מוציא others unless he ate a כזית of grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: But to fulfill the obligation of the many for them, he cannot do so until he eats an olive-size amount of grain.
steps.whatsHappening: The same statement now adds a limit. Joining is easy, but leading ברכת המזון on behalf of others requires a real grain meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two levels here. Joining the group needs only a small amount of food. Being מוציא others needs the person to be personally obligated in ברכת המזון, which requires a כזית of grain.

keyTerms.meaning: To fulfill the obligation for others
An olive-size amount, a basic halachic measure

steps.whatToRemember: Joining a זימון needs only a little food. Being מוציא others needs a כזית of grain.

phrases.english: And to fulfill the obligation of the many —
he does not fulfill it for them
until he eats an olive-bulk of grain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the same statement by limiting it: joining is allowed, but being מוציא others is not.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: To be מוציא others in ברכת המזון, one must have eaten a כזית of grain.

steps.title: The final הלכה: a vegetable leaf and wine let him join, but not lead
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that someone who ate a vegetable leaf and drank wine joins the זימון, but can be מוציא others only with a כזית of grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנא בר יהודה said in the name of רבא: The הלכה is that if he ate a vegetable leaf and drank a cup of wine, he joins. But to be מוציא others, he cannot until he eats a כזית of grain.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא gives the practical ruling (הלכתא) on this topic. It matches the two-level rule we just learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא uses a different example, a vegetable leaf and wine, but reaches the same split. Such a person joins the group, but cannot be מוציא others without a כזית of grain.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical ruling: a person who ate a little non-bread food can be counted for a זימון, but should not lead it for others.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חָנָא בַּר יְהוּדָה מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Ḥana bar Yehuda said in the name of Rava:
The halakha is: if he ate a vegetable leaf
and drank a cup of wine — he joins.
To fulfill others' obligation — he does not fulfill it
until he eats an olive-bulk of grain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חָנָא בַּר יְהוּדָה מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא: הִלְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final practical ruling on the topic of steps 1-2.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A vegetable leaf and wine let a person join a זימון. Being מוציא others requires a כזית of grain.

steps.title: משה instituted the first ברכה when the מן fell
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן begins a history of ברכת המזון: משה instituted ברכת הזן when the מן came down.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: משה instituted for Israel the ברכה of 'הזן' at the time the מן came down for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: the origin of each of the four ברכות of ברכת המזון. This step covers the first ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברכה thanks ה׳ for feeding everyone. It began when ה׳ fed the Jews with מן in the desert, so it was natural for משה to institute it then.

keyTerms.meaning: The first ברכה of ברכת המזון: 'Who feeds all'
The manna that fell in the desert

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said:
Moses instituted for Israel the blessing of 'Who feeds'
at the time the manna came down for them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: מֹשֶׁה תִּקֵּן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, the historical origins of the ברכות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ברכת הזן was instituted by משה when the מן fell.

steps.title: יהושע instituted the ברכה about the land
steps.stepSummary: יהושע instituted ברכת הארץ when the Jews entered ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: יהושע instituted for them the ברכה of the land once they entered the land.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן continues his list. Now he gives the source of the second ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second ברכה thanks ה׳ for ארץ ישראל. It fits that יהושע, who led the people into the land, instituted it.

keyTerms.meaning: The second ברכה, thanking ה׳ for ארץ ישראל ('נודה לך')

phrases.english: Joshua instituted for them the blessing of the land
once they entered the land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב נחמן's list with the second ברכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ברכת הארץ was instituted by יהושע upon entering the land.

steps.title: דוד and שלמה instituted בונה ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: The third ברכה came from two kings: דוד added the part about Israel and ירושלים, and שלמה added the part about the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: דוד and שלמה instituted 'בונה ירושלים'. דוד instituted 'on Israel Your people and on ירושלים Your city', and שלמה instituted 'on the great and holy House'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives the source of the third ברכה. He explains that it was built in two stages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד captured ירושלים, so he added the words about the city. שלמה built the בית המקדש, so he added the words about the Holy House. Each king added the part that matched what he accomplished.

keyTerms.meaning: The great and holy House, the בית המקדש

phrases.english: David and Solomon instituted 'Who builds Jerusalem'.
David instituted
'on Israel Your people and on Jerusalem Your city',
and Solomon instituted
'on the great and holy House'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list with the third ברכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בונה ירושלים was instituted in stages by דוד and שלמה.

steps.title: The fourth ברכה was instituted in יבנה because of ביתר
steps.stepSummary: הטוב והמטיב was instituted by the חכמים in יבנה in connection with the people killed at ביתר.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'הטוב והמטיב' was instituted in יבנה in reference to those killed at ביתר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן finishes his list with the fourth ברכה. Unlike the first three, it was instituted by the חכמים, not by a biblical leader.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברכה is later and rabbinic. It is tied to the massacre at ביתר at the end of the בר כוכבא revolt. The next step will explain the connection.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Who is good and does good', the fourth ברכה
The town where the סנהדרין sat after the חורבן

phrases.english: 'Who is good and does good' — they instituted it at Yavne
in reference to the slain of Beitar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list with the fourth ברכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הטוב והמטיב was instituted in יבנה because of the dead of ביתר.

steps.title: רב מתנא explains the two words of the fourth ברכה
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנא says the ברכה was instituted on the day the dead of ביתר were finally buried. 'הטוב' thanks ה׳ that the bodies did not decay, and 'המטיב' thanks Him that they were buried.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב מתנא said: On the day the dead of ביתר were allowed burial, they instituted 'הטוב והמטיב' in יבנה. 'הטוב' is for the fact that the bodies did not rot, and 'המטיב' is for the fact that they were brought to burial.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a statement of רב מתנא to support and explain the claim that the fourth ברכה is linked to ביתר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברכה's two words match two separate kindnesses. The bodies lay unburied for a long time but miraculously did not decay, which is 'הטוב'. In the end the Romans allowed them to be buried, which is 'המטיב'.

keyTerms.meaning: As (so-and-so) said, introducing a supporting source
They were given over for burial

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that even a ברכה of thanks can be rooted in a tragedy. The Jews found ה׳'s kindness even within destruction.

phrases.english: As Rav Mattana said:

phrases.aramaic: אוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם שֶׁנִּיתְּנוּ הֲרוּגֵי בֵּיתָר לִקְבוּרָה
phrases.english: On that day that the slain of Beitar were given over for burial
they instituted at Yavne 'Who is good and does good'.
'Who is good' — that they did not decompose,
'and does good' — that they were given over for burial.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports and explains step 7's link between the fourth ברכה and ביתר.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that הטוב והמטיב was instituted because of the dead of ביתר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב מתנא's statement about the day of burial and the meaning of each word.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists the order of the four ברכות
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא states the order: הזן, then ברכת הארץ, then בונה ירושלים, then הטוב והמטיב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: The order of ברכת המזון is as follows. The first ברכה is 'הזן', the second is ברכת הארץ, the third is 'בונה ירושלים', and the fourth is 'הטוב והמטיב'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that sets out the official order of the four ברכות. It is setting up a מחלוקת about שבת that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we have the fixed sequence of the ברכות, not just their history. This order is needed to understand where the שבת addition belongs.

keyTerms.meaning: The blessings recited after a bread meal

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
The order of Grace after Meals is as follows:
The first blessing — the blessing of 'Who feeds',
the second — the blessing of the land,
the third — 'Who builds Jerusalem',
the fourth — 'Who is good and does good',

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן, סֵדֶר בִּרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן כָּךְ הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the history of the ברכות to their fixed order.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The order is הזן, הארץ, בונה ירושלים, הטוב והמטיב.

steps.title: On שבת, mention the day inside the ברכה of comfort
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא says that on שבת, the third ברכה opens and closes with comfort for ירושלים, and שבת is mentioned in the middle.
steps.simpleTranslation: On שבת, one begins with comfort, ends with comfort, and says the holiness of the day in the middle.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא's first opinion (the תנא קמא) tells us where to add the שבת mention. It goes in the middle of the third ברכה, בונה ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The third ברכה is called 'נחמה' (comfort) because it asks for the rebuilding of ירושלים. On שבת, the שבת insert (רצה) is placed inside it, between its opening and its closing.

keyTerms.meaning: Comfort, here the name for the third ברכה (בונה ירושלים)
The holiness of the day, the mention of שבת

steps.confusionAlert: 'נחמה' here is not a separate ברכה. It is another name for the third ברכה, בונה ירושלים.

phrases.english: And on Shabbat — he begins with consolation
and ends with consolation,
and says the sanctity of the day in the middle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with the שבת rule (the תנא קמא's view).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שבת mention goes in the middle of the third ברכה.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: שבת may be mentioned in any of three ברכות
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר allows the שבת mention in the ברכה of comfort, in ברכת הארץ, or in the ברכה instituted in יבנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: If he wants to say it in the ברכה of comfort, he says it there. In ברכת הארץ, he says it there. In the ברכה the חכמים instituted in יבנה, he says it there.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the ברייתא gives much more flexibility about where to place the שבת mention.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר, the location is the person's choice among three ברכות. Only the first ברכה, הזן, is left out.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
If he wishes to say it in the consolation — he says it,
in the blessing of the land — he says it,
in the blessing the Sages instituted at Yavne — he says it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: רָצָה לְאוֹמְרָהּ בַּנֶּחָמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא by allowing three possible locations.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שבת mention may go in the third, second, or fourth ברכה.

steps.title: The חכמים: only in the ברכה of comfort
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say the שבת mention may be said only in the ברכה of comfort.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: He says it only in the ברכה of comfort.
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion in the ברייתא limits the שבת mention to the third ברכה alone. This sets up the גמרא's next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים reject רבי אליעזר's flexibility. But their view sounds just like the תנא קמא's, which raises a problem the גמרא will now ask about.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
He says it only in the consolation alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֵינוֹ אוֹמְרָהּ אֶלָּא בַּנֶּחָמָה בִּלְבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי אליעזר and seems to repeat the תנא קמא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שבת mention may only be said in the third ברכה.

steps.title: Aren't the חכמים saying the same thing as the תנא קמא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא records the חכמים separately, when they seem identical to the תנא קמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים are the same as the תנא קמא?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: two opinions seem to say exactly the same thing. Why list both?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא should not record the same view twice. Both the תנא קמא and the חכמים put שבת in the third ברכה, so there must be some difference between them.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה or ברייתא

phrases.english: The Rabbis — that is the same as the first tanna?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא's apparent redundancy between steps 10 and 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's recording of the חכמים as a separate opinion.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both opinions seem to place שבת only in the third ברכה, so recording both seems redundant.

steps.title: The difference is בדיעבד
steps.stepSummary: Both agree that one should mention שבת in the third ברכה. They differ about someone who already said it in a different ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them בדיעבד, after the fact.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The two opinions agree on what to do לכתחילה, but they disagree about what happens בדיעבד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא gives the ideal practice, the third ברכה. But if someone mentioned שבת in another of רבי אליעזר's ברכות, the תנא קמא holds he is still יוצא. The חכמים's word 'בלבד' teaches that only the third ברכה works, even בדיעבד.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them
After the fact, once it was already done

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא and the חכמים agree that שבת belongs in בונה ירושלים לכתחילה. They differ only on whether saying it elsewhere is valid בדיעבד.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the תנא קמא agrees fully with רבי אליעזר. He agrees with him only בדיעבד. לכתחילה he requires the third ברכה.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them — after the fact.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the redundancy question of step 13.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנא קמא and the חכמים hold exactly the same view.
steps.terutzMaskana: They agree לכתחילה. The תנא קמא accepts other ברכות בדיעבד, while the חכמים do not.

steps.title: Where Does the תורה Command ברכת המזון?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא opens by asking for the Torah source of ברכת המזון.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: From where do we know that ברכת המזון comes from the תורה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new ברייתא with a question: where is ברכת המזון in the תורה? This line sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the sugya dealt with the wording of the ברכות. Now it steps back and asks what the base source of the whole obligation is. The question assumes the obligation is דאורייתא and only asks where the פסוק is.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
From where do we know that Grace after Meals is from the Torah?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new ברייתא about the תורה source of ברכת המזון.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that serves as the source of ברכת המזון.

steps.title: Each Blessing Is Found in One Verse
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא matches each phrase of ״וְאָכַלְתָּ וְשָׂבָעְתָּ וּבֵרַכְתָּ״ to one ברכה of ברכת המזון.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says, "You shall eat, be satisfied, and bless." "Bless" is the ברכה of הזן. "ה׳ your God" is the ברכה of זימון. "For the land" is ברכת הארץ. "The good" is בונה ירושלים, since another פסוק calls ירושלים "this good mountain and the לבנון." "That He gave you" is הטוב והמטיב.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question by splitting one פסוק into pieces. Each piece is the source for a different ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this view every part of ברכת המזון, even זימון and הטוב והמטיב, has a hint in the תורה. The word "good" is linked to ירושלים through a second פסוק that uses the same word for הר הבית.

keyTerms.meaning: You shall eat, be satisfied, and bless
The first ברכה: Who feeds all
The invitation to bless together when three ate
The third ברכה: Who builds Jerusalem
The fourth ברכה: Who is good and does good

phrases.english: As it says: "And you shall eat and be satisfied, and you shall bless"
this is the blessing of "Who feeds"
"The Lord your God" is the zimmun blessing
"For the land" is the blessing of the land
"The good" is "Who builds Jerusalem"
and so it also says
"This good mountain and the Lebanon"
phrases.notes: Understood as הר הבית in ירושלים.

phrases.english: "That He gave you" is "Who is good and does good"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Every ברכה of ברכת המזון, including זימון and הטוב והמטיב, is learned from a phrase in דברים 8:10.

steps.title: What About a Blessing Before Eating?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks where we learn the ברכה said before eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: So far I only have a source for a ברכה after eating. From where do we know to make one before eating?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא notices that the פסוק only covers the ברכה after the meal. It asks for a source for the ברכה before, and this sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "eat, be satisfied, and bless" describe a ברכה after eating is finished. So the ברכה before eating still needs its own source.

phrases.english: I only have a source for after eating;
from where do we know before eating?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא לְאַחֲרָיו לְפָנָיו מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the search from the ברכה after eating to the ברכה before eating.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source for making a ברכה before eating.

steps.title: A Hungry Person Should Surely Bless
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא learns the ברכה before eating through a קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can say a קל וחומר: if a person blesses when he is full, then when he is hungry, all the more so.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers with logic instead of a פסוק. If one blesses after he is satisfied, he should surely bless when he is hungry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that a hungry person who is about to get food has even more reason to thank ה׳ than someone who is already full. So the ברכה before eating is learned from the ברכה after.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a lighter case to a stronger one
Is it not all the more so?

phrases.english: You can say it through an a fortiori argument:
When he is full, he blesses;
when he is hungry, is it not all the more so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברכה before eating is learned by קל וחומר from the ברכה after eating.

steps.title: רבי Reads the Verse Differently
steps.stepSummary: רבי agrees about הזן, ברכת הארץ and בונה ירושלים. But he learns זימון from a different פסוק, and says הטוב והמטיב was set up by the חכמים in יבנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: There is no need to read it that way. "Eat, be satisfied, and bless" is the ברכה of הזן. זימון is learned from "Praise ה׳ with me." "For the land" is ברכת הארץ. "The good" is בונה ירושלים, as it says "this good mountain and the לבנון." הטוב והמטיב was set up in יבנה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי gives a different reading of the same פסוק. He takes זימון and הטוב והמטיב out of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי, זימון comes from a פסוק in תהלים, "Praise ה׳ with me," which speaks of a group praising together. הטוב והמטיב has no תורה source at all, because the חכמים of יבנה added it. This leaves "that He gave you" free for a new use in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not needed (that reading or source)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי does not remove the obligation of זימון. He only learns it from a different פסוק. The only ברכה he treats as rabbinic is הטוב והמטיב.

phrases.english: Rebbi says: It is not needed:
"And you shall eat and be satisfied, and you shall bless" is the blessing of "Who feeds"
but the zimmun blessing
is derived from "Praise the Lord with me."
"For the land" is the blessing of the land
"The good" is "Who builds Jerusalem"

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר ״הָהָר הַטּוֹב הַזֶּה וְהַלְּבָנוֹן״.
phrases.english: and so it says: "This good mountain and the Lebanon."
"Who is good and does good" was instituted in Yavne.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with how step 16 reads the פסוק for זימון and הטוב והמטיב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: זימון comes from ״גַּדְּלוּ לַה׳ אִתִּי״, and הטוב והמטיב is a rabbinic ברכה from יבנה.

steps.title: רבי Also Asks About Before Eating
steps.stepSummary: Within רבי's view, the same question comes up again: where is the ברכה before eating?
steps.simpleTranslation: I only have a source for after eating. From where do we know before eating?
steps.whatsHappening: The same question from step 17 is asked again, this time inside רבי's approach. It sets up רבי's own answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is the same, but רבי will answer it differently. Since "that He gave you" is no longer used for הטוב והמטיב, he can use it here.

phrases.english: I only have a source for after eating;
from where do we know before eating?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא לְאַחֲרָיו לְפָנָיו מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the question of step 17 within רבי's reading.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי's source for the ברכה before eating.

steps.title: Bless From the Moment He Gave It
steps.stepSummary: רבי learns the ברכה before eating from the words "that He gave you": you must bless from the moment the food was given.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says "that He gave you," meaning from the moment He gave it to you.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי answers with a פסוק instead of a קל וחומר. He uses the words "that He gave you."
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי did not use "that He gave you" for הטוב והמטיב, he reads it as a time marker. The duty to bless starts as soon as the food is given, which is before one eats.

keyTerms.meaning: From the time He gave it to you

phrases.english: The verse teaches: "That He gave you"
from when He gave it to you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20 using the phrase that רבי freed up in step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "That He gave you" means one must bless from the moment the food is given, which is before eating.

steps.title: רבי יצחק: Bread Is Bread Before You Eat It
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק learns the ברכה before eating from ״וּבֵרַךְ אֶת לַחְמְךָ״, read as "and you shall bless". Food is called "bread" only before it is eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק says: That is not needed. The פסוק says "He will bless your bread and your water." Do not read it "He will bless." Read it "you shall bless." And when is it called "bread"? Before it is eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק offers a different source for the ברכה before eating. He uses a reading of a פסוק in שמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He rereads the vowels so the פסוק becomes a command for people to bless their bread. Since food is called "bread" only before it is eaten, the ברכה must come before eating.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not read (a homiletic change of vowels)
And you shall bless (instead of וּבֵרַךְ, "and He will bless")

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak says: It is not needed,
for it says
"And He will bless your bread and your water"
Do not read "and He will bless" but "and you shall bless."
And when is it called "bread"?
Before one eats it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a third source for the ברכה before eating.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברכה before eating comes from ״וּבָרֵךְ אֶת לַחְמְךָ״, since food is "bread" only before it is eaten.

steps.title: רבי נתן: שמואל Blessed Before the People Ate
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן learns the ברכה before eating from the story of שמואל. The people would not eat until he blessed the sacrifice.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נתן says: That is not needed. The פסוק says: "When you come into the city, you will find him before he goes up to the high place to eat. The people will not eat until he comes, because he blesses the sacrifice. After that, those who are invited eat."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נתן brings a story from נביאים that clearly shows a ברכה said before a meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this source the ברכה before eating is stated openly, with no logic and no rereading needed. The people waited to eat until שמואל blessed, which shows that the ברכה comes first.
steps.whatToRemember: There are four views on the ברכה before eating: the תנא קמא uses a קל וחומר, רבי uses "that He gave you," רבי יצחק uses "you shall bless your bread," and רבי נתן uses the story of שמואל. רבי also holds that הטוב והמטיב was set up in יבנה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Natan says: It is not needed,
for it says
"As soon as you come into the city, you will find him
before he goes up to the high place to eat

phrases.aramaic: כִּי לֹא יֹאכַל הָעָם עַד בֹּאוֹ
phrases.english: for the people will not eat until he comes
because he will bless the sacrifice
and afterward those who are invited will eat."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a fourth source for the ברכה before eating.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברכה before eating is shown in שמואל א 9:13, where the people waited for שמואל to bless before they ate.

steps.title: Why did the maidens talk so much?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the young women in the story of שמואל gave שאול such a long, drawn-out answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why all of that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses on a side detail from the story of שמואל it just quoted: why did the maidens give such a long answer? This question sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, שאול asked the girls a short question: is the seer here? They answered at great length. The גמרא wants to know the reason for all those extra words.

keyTerms.meaning: And why so much? Why all of that?

steps.confusionAlert: This is a side point (a tangent). It is not about ברכות. The main topic picks up again in step 28.

phrases.english: And why all of that (so much talking)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes a side question about the story quoted by רבי נתן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the maidens answered שאול at such length.

steps.title: Because women talk a lot
steps.stepSummary: First answer: women tend to talk a lot.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because women are talkative.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer says the long reply was simply the natural talkative way of the women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer finds no hidden meaning in the extra words. It explains them as ordinary human behavior.

phrases.english: Because women are talkative.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The women were by nature talkative.

steps.title: To look at שאול's beauty
steps.stepSummary: שמואל (the אמורא) says they kept talking so they could keep looking at שאול, who was very handsome and tall.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: In order to gaze at the beauty of שאול, as it is written: "From his shoulders and up he was taller than all the people."
steps.whatsHappening: The אמורא שמואל gives a second reason. The girls stretched out the talk so they could keep looking at שאול's beauty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He supports this from a פסוק that describes שאול as taller than everyone by a head. On this view the long answer had a purpose: to keep him there longer.
steps.confusionAlert: This שמואל is the אמורא שמואל. He is not שמואל הנביא from the story.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
In order to gaze at Saul's beauty,
as it is written: "From his shoulders and up he was taller than all the people."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different answer to step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: They spoke at length so they could look at שאול longer.

steps.title: One kingdom cannot overlap another
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the delay came from Heaven, so that שאול's rule would not start before שמואל's time was finished.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: Because one kingship may not touch its fellow, even by a hair's breadth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a third reason. The long talk delayed שאול so that his kingship would not cut into שמואל's leadership even a tiny bit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each leader has a fixed time. One leader's time cannot overlap with the next one's, not even by a hair. So Heaven arranged the delay to keep the two periods separate.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a famous principle: each leader has a set time that no one else can take.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Because one kingship does not touch its fellow
even by a hair's breadth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third answer to step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The delay kept שאול's reign from overlapping with שמואל's leadership.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three reasons for the long talk: women are talkative, they wanted to look at שאול, and one kingship cannot overlap another.

steps.title: Where do we learn ברכת התורה?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא goes back to its main topic. So far we have a source for ברכת המזון, but where do we learn ברכת התורה?
steps.simpleTranslation: I only have a source for ברכת המזון. From where do we learn ברכת התורה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the side story and goes back to the ברייתא about ברכות. It asks for a source for the ברכה said before learning תורה. The answers come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק we have been using only speaks about food and the land. A new source is needed to show that we also bless over תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we learn it?

phrases.english: I only have Grace after Meals.
From where do we learn the blessing of the Torah?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the side story to the ברייתא's list of sources.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל says: if we bless over food, which gives life for a short time, then surely we bless over תורה, which gives eternal life.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל said: It is a קל וחומר. If one blesses over temporary life, then surely one blesses over the life of עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל answers with a קל וחומר, an argument from the lesser to the greater.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food keeps us alive only for now, and still we bless over it. תורה gives eternal life, so it surely needs a ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Argument from the lesser to the greater
Eternal life of the World to Come

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael said: It is an a fortiori argument,
over temporary life one blesses,

phrases.aramaic: עַל חַיֵּי עוֹלָם הַבָּא לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן.
phrases.english: over the life of the World to Come, all the more so!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קל וחומר from ברכת המזון.

steps.title: No need for a קל וחומר: the word "gave"
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר נחמני, in the name of רבי ישמעאל, learns ברכת התורה from the matching word "gave" in two פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר נחמני, the student of רבי ישמעאל, says in the name of רבי ישמעאל: It is not needed. The פסוק says "for the good land which He gave you", and elsewhere it says "And I will give you the tablets of stone, and the Torah and the commandment".
steps.whatsHappening: A student of רבי ישמעאל says the קל וחומר is not needed. ברכת התורה can be learned from the same פסוק as ברכת המזון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The land is called something God "gave" (נתן), and the תורה is also called something God "will give" (ואתנה). The same word links the two: just as the gift of the land needs a ברכה, so does the gift of the תורה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya bar Nachmani,
the student of Rabbi Yishmael,
says in the name of Rabbi Yishmael:
It is not needed,
for it says
"for the good land which He gave you,"
and elsewhere it says:
"And I will give you the stone tablets,
and the Torah and the commandment, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר נַחְמָנִי תַּלְמִידוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different source and says the קל וחומר of step 29 is unnecessary.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ברכת התורה is learned from the word "gave", which is used both for the land and for the תורה.

steps.title: We bless on bad things too
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר learns from "ה׳ אלהיך" that we bless God for bad things just as we bless Him for good things.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: From where do we learn that just as one blesses over good, so one blesses over bad? The פסוק says "which ה׳ אלהיך gave you": your Judge, in every judgment He judges you, whether a measure of good or a measure of punishment.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר uses the same פסוק to teach that a person must bless God even when something bad happens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name אלהיך refers to God as Judge. So the gift is whatever God judges for you, good or bad. Either way, one blesses Him.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for blessing over bad news (דיין האמת) and for accepting God's judgment.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
And from where do we learn that just as one blesses over the good,
so too one blesses over the bad?

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״אֲשֶׁר נָתַן לְךָ ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ״,
phrases.english: The verse teaches: "which the Lord your God gave you",
(meaning) your Judge, in every judgment that He judges you,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין מִדָּה טוֹבָה וּבֵין מִדַּת פּוּרְעָנוּת.
phrases.english: whether a measure of good or a measure of punishment.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: וּמִנַּיִן שֶׁכְּשֵׁם שֶׁמְּבָרֵךְ עַל הַטּוֹבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Learns a new law from the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One must bless God over bad events just as over good ones.

steps.title: "Good" means תורה, and "the good" means ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בן בתירא learns both ברכת התורה and בונה ירושלים from the single word "הטובה".
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בן בתירא says: It is not needed. The פסוק says "good" and "the good". "Good" is תורה, as it says "for I gave you good teaching". "The good" is the building of ירושלים, as it says "this good mountain and the Lebanon".
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה בן בתירא says no other פסוק is needed. The word "הטובה" itself teaches both ברכת התורה and the ברכה about ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He splits the word into "טובה" and the extra ה of "הטובה". "טוב" is used for תורה in משלי, and "הטוב" is used for the mountain of the בית המקדש in ירושלים.

keyTerms.meaning: The good mountain (the site of the בית המקדש)
And so it says (a supporting פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: There are several sources for ברכת התורה: רבי ישמעאל's קל וחומר, the word "gave" (נתן / ואתנה), and "טובה" in the view of רבי יהודה בן בתירא. רבי מאיר adds that we bless on bad things too.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says:
It is not needed, for it says
"good", "the good".
"Good" is the Torah,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר: ״כִּי לֶקַח טוֹב נָתַתִּי לָכֶם״.
phrases.english: and so it says: "For I have given you good teaching."
"The good" is the building of Jerusalem,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר ״הָהָר הַטּוֹב הַזֶּה וְהַלְּבָנוֹן״.
phrases.english: and so it says: "this good mountain and the Lebanon."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא אוֹמֵר: אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers yet another source for ברכת התורה, from the word "הטובה".
steps.mimraCoreRuling: "טובה" teaches ברכת התורה, and "הטובה" teaches בונה ירושלים.

steps.title: Required wording for ברכת הארץ and בונה ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר rules that one who leaves out 'ארץ חמדה טובה ורחבה' in ברכת הארץ, or מלכות בית דוד in בונה ירושלים, has not fulfilled his obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי אליעזר says: Anyone who did not say 'a desirable, good, and spacious land' in the blessing of the land, and the kingdom of the house of David in 'Who builds Jerusalem,' has not fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about the exact wording of ברכת המזון. רבי אליעזר names specific phrases that must be included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps asked where we learn each blessing from. Now the question is what each blessing must contain. רבי אליעזר says leaving out these phrases makes the blessing not count, so they are required parts of the blessing.

keyTerms.meaning: A desirable, good, and spacious land (required praise of ארץ ישראל)
The blessing of the land (the second blessing of ברכת המזון, 'נודה לך')
The kingdom of the house of David
He has not fulfilled his obligation

steps.whyThisMatters: This is why our ברכת המזון says 'ארץ חמדה טובה ורחבה' in נודה לך and 'ועל מלכות בית דוד משיחך' in רחם.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
Anyone who did not say
'a desirable, good, and spacious land'
in the blessing of the land,
and the kingdom of the house of David in 'Who builds Jerusalem' —
phrases.notes: The words 'did not say' from phrase 2 carry over to this part too.

phrases.english: has not fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the sources of the blessings (steps 28-32) to the required wording inside them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leaving out 'ארץ חמדה טובה ורחבה' in ברכת הארץ, or מלכות בית דוד in בונה ירושלים, means the obligation is not fulfilled.

steps.title: נחום הזקן requires mentioning ברית
steps.stepSummary: נחום הזקן says ברכת הארץ must also mention the covenant of ברית מילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: נחום הזקן says: One must mention the covenant in it.
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא in the same ברייתא adds another required item to ברכת הארץ: the ברית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'בה' (in it) refers to ברכת הארץ. The 'ברית' is ברית מילה, which is linked to the land, since ארץ ישראל was promised to אברהם together with the covenant of מילה.
steps.confusionAlert: 'בה' means ברכת הארץ, not בונה ירושלים, even though בונה ירושלים was mentioned last.

phrases.english: Nachum the Elder says:
One must mention the covenant in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another required element to ברכת הארץ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ברכת הארץ must mention ברית מילה.

steps.title: רבי יוסי requires mentioning תורה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says ברכת הארץ must mention the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: One must mention the Torah in it.
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion adds that ברכת הארץ must also mention the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same wording is used as נחום הזקן, but with a new item. The list of required content in ברכת הארץ keeps growing: the land's praise, then ברית, now תורה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
One must mention the Torah in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds תורה as another required element, using the same wording as נחום הזקן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ברכת הארץ must mention the תורה.

steps.title: פלימו says ברית must come before תורה
steps.stepSummary: פלימו rules that ברית must be mentioned before תורה, because the תורה was given with only three covenants. His reason continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: פלימו says: He must put the covenant before the Torah, because this (the Torah) was given with three covenants,
steps.whatsHappening: פלימו accepts both ברית and תורה, but adds a rule about their order: ברית comes first. He begins to explain why, and the explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new point here is order, not just content. His reason compares the two: the תורה was given with three covenants. The next passage will show that מילה was given with thirteen covenants, so ברית is more weighty and should come first.
steps.whyThisMatters: Our נוסח follows this order: 'ועל בריתך שחתמת בבשרנו' comes before 'ועל תורתך שלמדתנו.'

phrases.english: Pelimo says:
He must put the covenant before the Torah,
because this (the Torah) was given with three covenants,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud, which compares this to מילה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the two previous opinions by setting the order between ברית and תורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In ברכת הארץ, ברית must be mentioned before תורה, because the תורה was given with only three covenants.
